title: Agent-supplied app status links can use unsafe URL schemes
summary:
### Summary

A workspace agent can attach a link to an app status update. Coder saved that link without checking its URL scheme and showed it as a clickable link in the dashboard. A malicious or compromised workspace could use this to show other users an unsafe link.

### Details

Workspace agents report app status through the agent API, which includes an optional `uri` field. Coder saved this value as sent and showed it as a link in the workspaces list and the workspace app status panel, and on releases before 2.38, in the task page header.

Any process in the workspace that holds the agent token can set this value. That includes an AI agent running a task, which could be steered by prompt injection.

The dashboard's Content Security Policy (`script-src 'self'`) stops `javascript:` links from running scripts in the Coder dashboard.

The fix makes the server keep status links only if they use `http`, `https` or `file`, and reject values with control characters. A disallowed link is dropped, but the status update is still saved.

### Impact

A user who controls a workspace agent, including an AI agent steered by prompt injection, can show an unsafe link to anyone who views that workspace or task, such as a template admin or a user it's shared with. A user who clicks it can be sent to a phishing site or a non-web application. The dashboard's Content Security Policy blocks `javascript:` links from running scripts in the Coder dashboard.

### Patches

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (Mainline) | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0) |
| 2.38 (Stable) | [v2.38.7](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.7) |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.11](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.11) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.19](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.19) |
| 2.29 (ESR) | [v2.29.27](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.27) |

Release lines 2.30 to 2.33, 2.35 and 2.36 are end-of-life. Users on any end-of-life line should upgrade to a patched release.

The fix applies to new status updates. Status links saved before upgrading are not changed and stay visible until the agent reports a new status.

App status links that use other schemes, such as `vscode://`, are no longer saved.

### Workarounds

There's no full workaround short of upgrading. Users should avoid clicking app status links from workspaces they don't trust.

### References

- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31262

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team and Jon David Black (@jondavid-black), who reported this independently.
